name: Chang'e 5-T1 (Xiaofei)
short_status: Circumlunar free-return flight test, 23 to 31 October 2014: the Xiaofei capsule proved the high-speed skip reentry for Chang'e 5 and landed in Inner Mongolia; the service module flew on to Earth-Moon L2 and then into lunar orbit.
tagline: CNSA · China · Flyby · 2014 · The robotic return Success
stats: reentry speed the skip maneuver had to survive, near Earth escape velocity
from launch to Xiaofei's touchdown in Inner Mongolia (8 d 4 h 42 m)
the 4M payload, first commercial spacecraft sent around the Moon
Chinese operation at the Earth-Moon L2 libration point

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 23 October 2014, 18:00 UTC, Long March 3C/G2 from Xichang Satellite Launch Center LC-2

facts.label: Purpose
facts.value: Preparatory flight test for Chang'e 5: validate atmospheric skip reentry of a capsule returning at lunar velocity, plus deep-space navigation and rendezvous rehearsal

facts.label: Spacecraft mass
facts.value: About 3,300 kg at launch; DFH-3A-derived service module, with a 335 kg return capsule (some accounts list a larger capsule mass)

facts.label: Trajectory
facts.value: Lunar free-return (circumlunar) flyby, no orbit insertion on the primary leg; closest approach roughly 12,000 to 13,000 km above the lunar far side on 28 October 2014

facts.label: Skip reentry
facts.value: Return capsule entered the atmosphere at better than 11 km/s, skipped back out to shed heat and speed, then reentered for a total reentry path of about 6,000 km, the technique later used by Chang'e 5 and Chang'e 6

facts.label: Capsule return
facts.value: Xiaofei (little flyer) landed 31 October 2014, 22:42 UTC (06:42 Beijing time, 1 November) in Siziwang Banner, Inner Mongolia, after a flight of 8 days, 4 hours, 42 minutes

facts.label: 4M commercial payload
facts.value: Manfred Memorial Moon Mission (4M), a 14 kg LuxSpace payload named for late OHB founder Manfred Fuchs, bolted to the Long March 3C upper stage; the first commercial payload ever flown around the Moon

facts.label: 4M radio beacon
facts.value: Transmitted JT65B digital messages on 145.980 MHz at 1.5 W; carried an iC-Malaga radiation dosimeter; received by more than 60 radio amateurs worldwide, transmitting until 11 November 2014, 01:35 UTC

facts.label: Service module to L2
facts.value: After capsule separation, the service module flew out to the Earth-Moon L2 point (China's first operation there), reaching a Lissajous parking orbit around L2 on 27 November 2014

facts.label: Service module to lunar orbit
facts.value: Departed L2 on 4 January 2015 and braked into a 5,300 by 200 km lunar orbit on 11 January 2015, later circularized near 200 km

facts.label: Chang'e 5 rehearsal
facts.value: In March 2015 the service module lowered to about 18 km altitude to rehearse Chang'e 5 rendezvous geometry, ran virtual-target docking tests, and imaged the candidate landing zone in Oceanus Procellarum

facts.label: Upper stage lunar impact (2022)
facts.value: The mission's Long March 3C upper stage is the leading identification for the object that struck the lunar far side on 4 March 2022, leaving an unusual double crater (18 m and 16 m, about 29 m across) at 5.226 N, 234.486 E near Hertzsprung basin; China disputed the attribution

timeline: Launch at 18:00 UTC on a Long March 3C/G2 from Xichang, carrying the 4M commercial payload on the upper stage
Free-return lunar flyby, closest approach roughly 12,000 to 13,000 km above the far side
Xiaofei capsule performs the skip reentry at better than 11 km/s and lands in Siziwang Banner, Inner Mongolia, at 22:42 UTC
The 4M payload sends its final transmission at 01:35 UTC after four times its design life
Service module reaches a Lissajous parking orbit around the Earth-Moon L2 point, a first for China
Service module departs L2 and brakes into lunar orbit
Service module descends to about 18 km to rehearse Chang'e 5 rendezvous geometry and image the Oceanus Procellarum landing zone
The mission's Long March 3C upper stage (leading identification) strikes the lunar far side, leaving a double crater near Hertzsprung basin
